correctness.rationale: Using the planar convex Cheeger characterization |(K_R)_{-t}|=pi*t^2 with unique t=1/h, independently derived eroded set [-1+t,1-t]^2 intersect B_(R-t). The clipped area 4a*sqrt(b²-a²)+4b²(asin(a/b)-pi/4) is correct in a<b<sqrt(2)a. Monotonicity of F_R(t) gives a unique root. Inner square fits the eroded disk at R*=sqrt(2)-(sqrt(2)-1)*2/(2+sqrt(pi)), establishing an exact constant-set plateau, while strict inclusion below R* increases t. Side-cap loss from four caps is (16/3)sqrt(2b)*(R-1)^(3/2)+O((R-1)^(5/2); the corner loss is 4d²+O(d³). These yield both stated asymptotic constants. Own 65-digit independent root/cap calculations checked intermediate radii and both limits; all checks passed. Endpoint R=1 gives h=2, R=sqrt(2) the rounded-square value. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof of continuum quantifiers.

value.rationale: The Cheeger set of a natural planar disk-to-square deformation becomes rigorously insensitive to further corner changes at a nontrivial sharp radius. Opposite endpoint tangencies yield 3/2 and 2 exponents with exact coefficients; the plateau is a motivated geometric stability phenomenon and an exact parametric classification, not merely a recalculation of the square endpoint.
